answer: An agent economy can require every identity to bond tokens in a public registry and let other agents challenge suspicious clusters. A successful challenge slashes the bond and pays part to the challenger; the rest can fund audits. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock real capital for each identity and risks losing it, while merely inventing names is insufficient. A voyage of linked accounts may share a funding trail, but a knoll of unrelated claims needs evidence; a cipher can protect private details without hiding the bond or challenge outcome.
